title: [Clinical outcomes of horse antithymocyte globulin-based immunosuppressive therapy for aplastic anemia at a single institution].
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: Horse antithymocyte globulin (hATG) has been available for the treatment of aplastic anemia (AA) in Japan since 2023. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of combination therapy with hATG, cyclosporine, and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA), and determine the optimal steroid regimen for serum sickness prophylaxis. We retrospectively reviewed seven patients with AA who received hATG combined with cyclosporine and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA; eltrombopag or romiplostim). The median age was 62 years. All patients achieved transfusion independence within 3 months (median day 35 for red blood cells and day 36 for platelets). Six patients remain alive and transfusion-independent, while one died of heart failure. The early dose-reduction regimen frequently failed because of serum sickness, necessitating a switch to the conventional method. hATG-based triple therapy led to rapid transfusion independence. Switching TPO-RAs may be effective in patients with a suboptimal response. The conventional method of steroid prophylaxis may be preferable.

title: Pregnancy outcome and associated factors following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
abstract: Colic surgery in pregnant broodmares raises concerns not only for maternal survival but also for fetal outcome. Although several studies have reported foaling rates after colic surgery and the influence of perioperative factors on pregnancy outcome, the findings remain inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the foaling rate following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares and to evaluate the effects of perioperative factors and gestational stage on pregnancy outcome. Medical records of Thoroughbred broodmares that underwent colic surgery at Shadai Horse Clinic from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Data collected included mare age, gestational stage, diagnosis category, intraoperative hypotension, hypoxemia, anesthetic maintenance technique (inhalation anesthesia alone or inhalation anesthesia combined with partial intravenous anesthesia), duration of general anesthesia, postoperative administration of altrenogest, postoperative complications (diarrhea and catheter-associated jugular phlebitis), postoperative signs of endotoxemia, and pregnancy outcome. The overall foaling rate was 69.6% (110/158). The occurrence of intraoperative hypotension in late-gestational mares (P=0.036) were significantly associated with negative pregnancy outcome in univariate analysis, whereas most other perioperative factors showed no significant association. The occurrence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly higher in the late-gestational mares, however it did not affect pregnancy outcome. In conclusion, the foaling rate following colic surgery in pregnant Thoroughbred broodmares was comparable to that reported in previous studies. These findings suggest that intraoperative hypotension may warrant particular attention in late-gestation mare undergoing colic surgery.

title: Evaluation of linkage disequilibrium, haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size in the Iranian Turkmen horse.
journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
abstract: This study used the Illumina Equine SNP70 BeadChip to investigate whole-genome linkage disequilibrium (LD), haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size (Ne) of the Iranian Turkmen horse. Genotyping was performed on 70 samples, of which 62 passed quality control and were retained for analysis. We estimated the extent of LD using r2 and D' measures and characterized haplotype block structure and historical Ne. Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify biological functions associated with genes within the detected haplotype blocks. Across all SNP pairs analyzed (distance ≤ 5 Mb), mean r2 was 0.04, while mean D' was 0.47. Mean r2 for the closest SNP pairs (<5 kb) was 0.49, indicating high LD at short distances. Because D' is sensitive to allele frequency and sample size, the interpretation focused primarily on r2. A total of 5,155 haplotype blocks were detected, mainly on chromosome 1, involving 16,553 SNPs and encompassing 29% of all SNPs in the genome. The estimated Ne decreased with increasing number of generations, indicating the need for adequate conservation measures to ensure the genetic diversity of this valuable breed. GO and pathway enrichment analysis of genes within the longest haplotype blocks showed significant overrepresentation of biological processes related to steroid metabolism, oxidative demethylation, apoptotic signaling, chemical carcinogenesis, and retinol metabolism. These findings suggest candidate biological processes that require further validation.

title: Ecdysterone concentrations in horses following treatment and withdrawal of this naturally occurring prohibited anabolic steroid.
abstract: The medicinal properties of ecdysterone, a steroid made by plants, insects, and internal parasites, have been exploited in traditional medicine for decades. As ecdysterone can increase muscle strength, it could benefit senior horses with muscle wasting. However, the wide availability of ecdysterone supplements is a concern for horseracing authorities, while the risk of environmental exposure to this prohibited substance presents a challenge for owners and trainers. This study examined ecdysterone concentrations in eight Standardbred horses following ecdysterone treatment, re-examined samples from another study using 17 horses, and compared ELISA values with mass spectrometry data to explore some unexpected results. Serum ecdysterone concentrations peaked at 36ng/mL (median), 40min after a single oral dose (5mg/kgBW). A second peak occurred, likely due to enterohepatic recycling, between 2 and 24h, varying markedly between horses and reaching 9 to 134ng/mL. Concentrations returned to pre-treatment values in all horses after 32h and no accumulation occurred in serum or faeces during 7 daily doses. Serum ecdysterone was persistently high (ca. 20ng/mL) in one individual when measured by ELISA, but not by mass spectrometry, indicating likely interference with the antibody-based assay. Otherwise, the two analytical methods showed good agreement. Ecdysterone concentrations measured in 17 different horses four times in one day showed marked and sporadic spikes which appeared and disappeared within 40min, suggesting an endogenous origin (e.g. from internal parasites). Additional studies are needed to understand this phenomenon, assist anti-doping authorities in setting a residue limit, and explore therapeutic opportunities in equine medicine.

title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7 ± 0.8 nM) as the standard reference inhibitor. IC50 values were determined, and inhibition constants (Kᵢ) were calculated via Lineweaver-Burk plot analysis. The ranked Kᵢ values were as follows: Haloperidol (2.80 ± 1.6 nM) < Ethacrynic acid (4.70 ± 0.8 nM) < Risperidone (4.90 ± 0.39 nM) < Fluoxetine hydrochloride (5.40 ± 1.0 nM) < Aripiprazole (6.10 ± 0.7 nM) < Sodium valproate (386.0 ± 0.0 nM). Haloperidol showed the strongest GST inhibition among the tested drugs, even exceeding ethacrynic acid in binding affinity. This suggests its potential as a GST modulator in cancer therapy. Molecular docking studies revealed that the highest binding affinities were observed for Risperidone and Aripiprazole, showing scores of -7.350 to -7.576 Kcal/mol for 9GSS and -8.786 to -8.982 Kcal/mol for 5JCU. These strong interactions indicate a high potential of both compounds to effectively bind within the GST active site. The molecular dynamics simulation confirmed the stability and consistency of these complexes throughout the simulation period. Given the anticancer role of GST inhibitors, psychotropic drugs with significant GST inhibition especially haloperidol may positively contribute to cancer treatment.

title: Metabolite profiling and in vitro biological activities of an endophytic Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 isolated from Origanum syriacum L.
abstract: Endophytic fungi associated with the za'atar plant (O. syriacum L.) remain largely underexplored despite their potential as sources of bioactive natural products. This study aimed to characterize the endophytic fungus Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 recovered from Origanum syriacum leaves and to investigate its chemical profile and biological activities. Identification of Cladosporium sp. was achieved by morphological and molecular approaches. Comprehensive metabolite profiling of the ethyl acetate (EtOAc) crude extract was conducted using complementary chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques, including gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). GC-MS analysis tentatively annotated 32 volatile and semi-volatile compounds based on mass spectral database matching and retention index comparison, predominantly monoterpenes, sesquiterpenes, and fatty alcohols. Targeted LC-MS/MS analysis detected 11 metabolites that were assigned based on retention time and mass-spectrometric characteristics in comparison with authentic reference standards. Several of these metabolites have not previously been reported in an endophytic Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum. The EtOAc crude extract exhibited moderate antioxidant activity in the DPPH assay (IC50 = 230.21 ± 5.96 μg/mL). It also showed low cytotoxic activity against HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells (IC50 = 93.43 μg/mL), with cell death involving both apoptotic and necrotic pathways. In addition, the extract displayed antibacterial activity against six bacterial species comprising five foodborne bacterial pathogens and one an opportunistic equine pathogen, with inhibition rates of 67.37% ± 2.45% against Staphylococcus aureus and 59.39% ± 1.24% against Campylobacter jejuni. Collectively, these findings indicate that Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum is a promising source of chemically diverse metabolites with potential biological activities.

title: In Vivo Metabolic Profiling of Suzetrigine in Thoroughbred Horses Following Oral Administration: Implications for Equine Anti-Doping Control.
abstract: Suzetrigine (VX-548), a selective NaV1.8 sodium channel blocker recently approved for pain management, was investigated for its metabolic fate in Thoroughbred horses using liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS). Equine urine and plasma samples were collected following administration and processed prior to analysis. Combining the present in vivo data with earlier reported in vitro liver incubations, a total of 12 metabolites (M1-M12) were identified and characterised, comprising nine Phase I and three Phase II biotransformation products. Five Phase I metabolites (M1-M4 and M9) were detected in vivo, formed through O-demethylation, C-demethylation, monohydroxylation, and hydrolysis of the amide function. Four further Phase I metabolites (M5-M8), previously reported by our team, were observed solely in in vitro liver incubations and were not detected in any in vivo sample. Phase II metabolism yielded three conjugated metabolites, comprising two glycosidation products (M10 and M11) detected in both urine and plasma, and one sulfonate conjugate (M12) confined to urine. Intact suzetrigine was the most abundant plasma analyte at every sampling point, followed by the O-demethylated metabolite M1, whereas in urine, the amide hydrolysis product M9 was overwhelmingly dominant and the parent drug accounted for less than 1% of its response. Intact suzetrigine remained detectable in plasma throughout a 192-h period, while M1 and M9 persisted in urine to the final sampling points. These findings define the metabolic disposition of suzetrigine in the horse and identify M9 and M1 as the most suitable analytical targets for the detection of suzetrigine misuse in equine doping control.

title: Evidence of Coxiella burnetii exposure in equids in Brazil.
abstract: Coxiella burnetii exposure in equids remains poorly investigated worldwide and has never been evaluated in Brazil. To investigate the occurrence of anti-C. burnetii antibodies in a large population of equids from southeastern Brazil and to identify associated risk factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 307 apparently healthy equids, including horses, donkeys, and mules, from six municipalities in the Greater Vitória Metropolitan Region, Espírito Santo State, Brazil. Sera were tested for anti-C. burnetii antibodies by indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA). Univariate analysis was performed to evaluate associations between seropositivity and demographic, environmental, and management variables. Seropositivity was detected in 9.45% (29/307) of the animals. A statistically significant association was observed between location and seropositivity (P = 0.0146), with equids from Vila Velha showing 4.26-fold higher odds of seropositivity than those from the reference municipality. Breeding equids showed higher odds of seropositivity (OR = 1.49), whereas equids with cat contact showed lower odds (OR = 0.45); however, neither association was statistically significant. No significant associations were observed between seropositivity and sex, age, equid type, topography, access to standing water, contact with ruminants, dogs, pigs, poultry, or tick infestation. This study provides the first evidence of exposure to C. burnetii in equids from Brazil. The absence of an association between seropositivity and contact with ruminants, together with the higher seropositivity observed in one municipality, suggests that exposure to C. burnetii may be more closely related to geographic area than to contact with known animal reservoirs.

title: A dietary nutraceutical "Succeed Digestive Conditioning ProgramTM" is more effective than omeprazole for managing equine glandular gastric disease.
abstract: Equine glandular gastric disease (EGGD) responds poorly to proton pump inhibitor therapy, highlighting the need for alternative treatments. Succeed Digestive Conditioning Program (SUC) contains oat-derived ingredients, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, L-glutamine, and L-threonine that may support gastric health. To compare effects of SUC and omeprazole (OME) on squamous and glandular gastric ulcers in horses. Fifty-nine horses with squamous gastric lesions (score ≥2/4) completed a 90-day trial. Horses received either OME (4 mg/kg BW/day; n=30) or SUC (27 g/day; n=29). Forty-four horses had concurrent glandular lesions (OME, n=21; SUC, n=23). Gastroscopy was performed on Days 0, 30, 60, and 90. Squamous lesions were graded using a 0-4 scoring system. Glandular lesions were evaluated using lesion number, lesion severity, and composite ulcer index. Fecal pH was also assessed. OME reduced squamous lesion scores by Day 30 (P<0.001), and scores were lower than SUC horses on Days 30 (P=0.007), 60 (P<0.001), and 90 (P=0.02). SUC had no effect on squamous lesion scores. SUC reduced glandular lesion number scores by Day 60 (P=0.003) and Day 90 (P=0.003), and reduced glandular ulcer index scores by Day 60 (P=0.01) and Day 90 (P=0.03). OME had no effects on any glandular metrics. Neither treatment affected fecal pH. Omeprazole effective reduced squamous gastric lesions but did not improve glandular lesions. In contrast, SUC improved glandular lesion number and ulcer index without affecting squamous disease. SUC may represent a useful strategy for managing EGGD and further investigation into clinical applications are warranted.

title: Physiological impact of reduced anthelmintic intervention in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals: identifying stress indicators of welfare significance.
abstract: Gastrointestinal parasitism is common in pasture-raised foals, yet fecal egg count (FEC) may not reflect its physiological impact. Reduced anthelmintic use therefore requires integrated indicators of health, stress, and resilience. To evaluate associations between FEC, growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), cortisol, and behavior-related observations in naturally infected Thoroughbred foals managed under selective anthelmintic control. Thirty-five foals were followed from birth to 13 months under extensive management in southern Brazil, yielding 348 monthly evaluations. Growth, clinical and behavioral responses, FEC, coproculture, hematology, NLR, serum cortisol, fecal consistency, and anthelmintic efficacy were assessed using nonparametric analyses. Cyathostomins predominated (84.0%), whereas Strongyloides spp. occurred mainly in summer. FEC ranged from 0 to 2,900 eggs/g and varied markedly among individuals. Body weight and wither height increased progressively, with average daily gain exceeding 1.0 kg/day during the first three months. Hematological values were mostly within reference ranges, and leukocyte abnormalities were infrequent (4.21%) and mild. Mean NLR was 1.56 ± 1.03. Cortisol was lower in treated foals (P < 0.001) but was not associated with FEC. No consistent associations were found between FEC and growth, hematology, leukocyte morphology, NLR, cortisol, or fecal consistency. Fecal egg count reduction was 6.6% after ivermectin plus praziquantel and 83.3% after piperazine. Foals maintained growth and physiological stability despite persistent subclinical parasitism. FEC alone was insufficient to indicate physiological or behavior-related impairment or the need for treatment.

title: The horse's hidden threat: occurrence and exposure risks to the tremorgenic alkaloid paxilline in central European grasslands.
abstract: Paxilline is a tremorgenic indole-diterpenoid produced by toxin-producing fungal endophytes in meadows and pastures. It is currently understudied in European grasslands. This study evaluated the occurrence of paxilline in selected European grasslands and estimated the exposure risks for horses. The risk of the paxilline exposure was estimated based on the analyses made from a total of 392 grass samples from grasslands. The grass species Lolium perenne, Lolium multiflorum, Festuca pratensis, Festuca arundinacea, Festuca rubra, Festuca nigrescens, and Festulolium × loliaceum were sampled from grasslands in Austria (n=42 samples, 1 location), France (n=134, 1 location), Hungary (n=14, 1 location), and Germany (n=192, 4 locations). Concentrations were determined using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Per location and year, the positive samples for paxilline ranged from 0 to 45% of tested samples. Associations with location and plant species were observed (p < 0.001). Model estimates using logistic procedures indicated high likelihoods (up to 75%) for detecting paxilline in certain grasslands, such as in France and Austria, especially for F. rubra, followed by L. multiflorum and L. perenne. Temperatures measured two months before sampling were more positively associated with the concentration of paxilline than that at sampling week. Horses are exposed to paxilline in central European grasslands, but the exposure risk differs with their location and plant species. The study suggests that besides preserving the biodiversity of grasslands, routine monitoring for alkaloid occurrence may be needed, especially when F. rubra, L. multiflorum and L. perenne are present.

title: Investigating horse owners' confidence, ability and knowledge-seeking behaviour in recognising equine lameness.
abstract: Undiagnosed lameness is common in horses, but little is known about which aspects of lameness identification owners find difficult. To explore horse owners' confidence and ability to identify equine lameness, and their knowledge-seeking behaviour. In this cross-sectional online survey, 509 UK horse/pony owners identified lameness from videos of sound, forelimb, hindlimb and bilaterally lame horses, reported their knowledge of clinical signs and knowledge-seeking behaviour, and rated their confidence (1, not confident at all, to 5, very confident). Mixed-effects logistic regression (respondent as random effect) tested whether confidence predicted correct identification. Correct identification was 50.6% (n=256/506) for the sound horse, 50.3% (n=510/1014) for forelimb lameness, 32.3% (n=326/1009) for hindlimb lameness, and 8.9% (n=45/505) for bilateral lameness. Confidence significantly predicted correct limb identification (odds ratio [OR] 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.43-1.70, P < 0.001), remaining significant after adjusting for case difficulty (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.30-1.58, P < 0.001), which was a stronger predictor. The most common clinical signs described were 'head nod' (93.7%, n=477/509) and 'hip hike/asymmetry' (77.2%, n=393/509); 'pain expressions' accounted for only 7.4% (n=75/1018) of responses. Owners' main information sources were personal experience (95.7%, n=487/509), vet (63.9%, n=325/509), and coach/trainer (23.6%, n=120/509). Many owners failed to correctly identify the affected limb in hindlimb and bilateral lameness, and rarely used signs such as pain expressions. Confidence significantly predicted correct identification, but case difficulty explained more of the variation in accuracy, highlighting a need for evidence-based resources targeted at less confident or less able owners.

title: Preliminary insights into the association between platelet indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares.
abstract: Endometritis is a major cause of subfertility in mares and is characterized by uterine inflammation and impaired uterine clearance. Platelets contribute to inflammation, immune regulation and tissue remodeling, and platelet (PLT) indices have emerged as readily available biomarkers of inflammatory conditions; however, their association with endometritis in mares remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the relationship between PLT indices and uterine inflammatory status in cyclic mares. Seventeen cyclic mares were classified into healthy (n = 10) and endometritis (n = 7) groups based on cytological evidence of endometrial inflammation and ultrasonographic detection of intrauterine fluid accumulation. Uterine inflammatory status was characterized by endometrial cytology and ultrasonographic findings, including intrauterine fluid accumulation and endometrial edema. PLT indices were measured using an automated hematology analyzer (ADVIA® 2120i), and plasma estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) concentrations were determined. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Mares with endometritis showed significantly higher PLT count, plateletcrit (PCT), mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet large cell ratio (P-LCR), platelet distribution width (PDW), mean platelet mass (MPM), platelet component distribution width (PCDW) and platelet mass distribution width (PMDW) than healthy mares. All significant differences remained after correction and exhibited large to very large effect sizes. In addition, mares with endometritis showed higher plasma E2 concentrations and lower P4 concentrations than healthy mares. These findings indicate that endometritis is associated with marked alterations in circulating PLT characteristics, particularly in indices related to PLT size, heterogeneity, and mass. PLT indices obtained from routine hematological analyses may represent accessible complementary biomarkers of uterine inflammatory status in mares.

title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
abstract: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses. To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR. Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe). Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests. Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected. Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity. Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR.

title: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation.
abstract: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively. In vitro assessment revealed divergent probiotic adaptive traits between the two strains, particularly in gastrointestinal stress tolerance. Genomic analysis revealed the presence of genes encoding the functionally related effector proteins P9 and Amuc_1100. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, supplementing with Muc_T9 and Mas_DA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and alleviated colonic inflammation and histological damage. Notably, divergent expression patterns of key genes involved in lipid metabolism and adipose tissue remodeling suggest potential differences in host metabolic regulatory modes. Furthermore, both strains restored gut microbial diversity and increased the relative abundance of putative short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing bacteria. Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.

title: A Paper-Based Electrochemiluminescence Lateral Flow Immunoassay Using Ruthenium Complex Labeling for the Detection of Naja Naja Venom.
abstract: An indirect competitive paper-based electrochemiluminescence (ECL) lateral flow immunoassay was developed for quantitative detection of Naja naja venom. Equine anti-Naja naja venom IgG served as the primary recognition antibody, ruthenium-complex-labeled rabbit anti-equine IgG as the ECL reporter and immobilized three-finger toxin (3FTX) as the competitive antigen. Ruthenium labeling conditions, the co-reactant system, detection membrane, membrane length, and the labeled-secondary-antibody-to-3FTX ratio were optimized. The selected conditions were a Ru-NHS (ruthenium-complex N-hydroxysuccinimide) ester-to-secondary-antibody molar ratio of 160:1 at 25 °C, Elecsys buffer as the co-reactant, Whatman AE 100 as a 1.5 cm detection membrane, and a 3000:1 secondary-antibody-to-3FTX concentration ratio. The whole-venom calibration series was fitted with a decreasing four-parameter logistic model (R2 = 0.9980). Blank-threshold analysis followed by six-run low-concentration verification supported a practical limit of detection of 32 ng/mL. Quantitative verification identified a limit of quantitation (LOQ) of 300 ng/mL and a validated quantitative range of 300-10,000 ng/mL. The within-batch coefficient of variation (CV) was 3.46%, and the coefficient of variation among three batch means was 1.63%. At 10,000 ng/mL, Naja naja venom produced a lower ECL response than Deinagkistrodon acutus venom, Bungarus multicinctus venom, serum, and phosphate-buffered saline controls. These findings support the analytical feasibility of the competitive paper-based ECL platform and provide a basis for further matrix, cross-reactivity, stability, and clinical-sample validation.

title: Effects of Low-Intensity Exercise on Exhaled Breath Condensate Biomarkers in Healthy Horses.
abstract: Exhaled breath condensate (EBC) has emerged as a promising diagnostic tool for equine respiratory disease. However, the influence of exercise on the biomarkers of EBC remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of low-intensity exercise on EBC biomarkers (hydrogen peroxide, pH, and nitrite) in healthy horses and to assess the feasibility of postexercise sample collection under real-world conditions. Twenty clinically healthy horses (ten Quarter Horses and ten Brazilian Sport Horses) were evaluated. Respiratory rate (RR) and heart rate (HR) were recorded at rest, followed by EBC collection using a collector developed by our research group. Horses then performed 10 min of trotting, low-intensity protocol, after which RR, HR, and EBC samples were reassessed. Upper airway endoscopy and tracheal lavage with differential cytology confirmed respiratory health. Biomarker concentrations were analyzed by using appropriate parametric tests. Light exercise significantly increased RR, HR, and EBC sample volumes (p < 0.05). Sample volume evidenced a weak association with ambient temperature (p = 0.014, r = 0.186) and relative humidity (p = 0.010, r = 0.218). Exercise did not significantly affect pH (p = 0.380), hydrogen peroxide (p = 0.152), or nitrite (p = 0.218). Nitrite was negatively associated with ambient temperature (p = 0.023, r = -0.056) and relative humidity (p < 0.001, r = -0.428) and evidenced a moderate positive association with hydrogen peroxide in postexercise (p = 0.004, r = 0.611). Under the conditions evaluated, light exercise did not alter equine EBC biomarker concentrations, supporting the feasibility of postexercise sampling.

title: Absolute Quantification of Tissue Composition by Raman Spectroscopy.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Raman spectroscopy captures the molecular fingerprints of living tissues without labels or tissue destruction. Translating these spectra into absolute measures of tissue biochemical composition remains a challenge owing to tissue-dependent optical properties, variations in sampling volume, and lack of normalization standards requisite for quantitative scaling. Here we introduce a scheme to derive the biochemical constituents of a tissue expressed as a percentage of the tissue wet weight, like biochemical assays, from Raman spectra measured optically. Nonlinear polynomial models of Raman spectra are trained on chemically defined phantoms that mimic the variability of the essential biochemical constituents of a tissue, accommodating spectral overlap and tissue-dependent optical effects. We validated this scheme using cartilage, a tissue fundamental to diarthrodial joint function. Cartilage is comprised of glycosaminoglycans, collagens and water that act synergistically to impart the rheological and tribological material properties essential to tissue function. Using biochemically perturbed live cartilage explants, phantom-calibrated Raman spectroscopy (PC-Raman) resolved constituent-specific changes and achieved quantitative agreement with independent biochemical assays (R2 = 0.88-0.92; slopes ≈ 1.0; 95% confidence intervals ±2.7-3.2%pt). We demonstrate that PC-Raman is applicable across the hierarchy of tissue interrogation from microscopic imaging of tissue extracellular matrix composition to macroscopic longitudinal monitoring of drug effects in-vitro using live tissue constructs and in-vivo assessments of cartilage regeneration in an equine cartilage repair model. Converting Raman spectra measurements of the essential biochemical constituents of a tissue in absolute terms (tissue wet-weight-%) allows for the non-destructive, longitudinal quantification of tissue composition in disease (tissue degeneration) and in response to treatment (tissue repair).

title: Clinical Outcomes and Safety of Tendon-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy in Equine Tendon and Ligament Injuries.
authors: de Pouyade G De La Rebière
abstract: Equine tendinopathies and desmopathies are common musculoskeletal disorders characterized by a limited regenerative capacity and a high risk of recurrence. Tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TDSCs) represent a promising regenerative therapy due to their immunomodulatory and pro-regenerative properties. This preliminary prospective clinical study aimed to evaluate the safety and potential efficacy of allogeneic post-mortem TDSCs, for the treatment of superficial digital flexor tendon (SDFT) and suspensory ligament (SL) injuries in horses. Nine horses were monitored longitudinally for up to 18 months following intralesional TDSC injection. Clinical outcome was assessed using subjective lameness evaluation, objective locomotion analysis with inertial sensors and standardized ultrasonographic examinations. The treatment was well tolerated, with no major adverse effects, supporting the low immunogenicity of allogeneic TDSCs. Overall clinical improvement was observed during the follow-up period and was consistent with improved locomotor symmetry measured objectively. Ultrasonographic findings suggested favorable tissue remodeling, including a reduction in hypoechoic lesions and progressive reorganization of the fibrillar architecture. However, treatment responses were heterogeneous, with SDFT lesions showing earlier clinical and ultrasonographic improvement than SL lesions. Nevertheless, this trend was not reflected in long-term outcomes, as only two horses, both presenting SL lesions, returned to their previous level of competition without reported recurrence. Allogeneic TDSCs appear to be a safe and promising therapeutic approach for equine tendon and ligament injuries. Nevertheless, their ability to reduce long-term recurrence remains uncertain and should be investigated in larger controlled clinical trials.

title: Impact of Suspensory Ligament Desmitis on Athletic Performance of Trotting Horses: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Suspensory ligament (SL) desmitis is one of the most common musculoskeletal injuries affecting trotting horses being frequently associated with reduced athletic performance and premature retirement. However, the prognostic value of clinical and ultrasonographic findings remains incompletely understood. To evaluate the impact of proximal and/or body SL desmitis on athletic performance of French Trotters and determine whether horse related characteristics, ultrasonographic lesion severity, lesion location, or treatment modality influence prognosis. Medical records of 36 French Trotters diagnosed with proximal and/or body SL desmitis were retrospectively reviewed. Horse related characteristics, ultrasonographic findings, treatment protocols, recurrence, inactivity period, return to competition, race earnings, and Index of Trot (ITR) were analysed. Statistics were applied with non-parametric testing. Twenty-four horses (66.7%) returned to competition, whereas 12 (33.3%) retired. Four horses experienced recurrence after returning to competition. The median inactivity period was 193 days. Age, number of affected limbs, lesion location, treatment modality, and ultrasonographic parameters (cross-sectional area grade, longitudinal fibre pattern, and overall lesion severity) did not significantly influence outcome, recurrence, or inactivity period (all p > 0.05). Post-injury race earnings (p = 0.005) and ITR values (p = 0.004) were significantly lower than pre-injury values. Hindlimb lesions were associated with a longer inactivity period than forelimb lesions (p = 0.03). SL desmitis significantly compromises athletic performance in French Trotters despite a relatively high return-to-competition rate. Common clinical and ultrasonographic variables showed limited prognostic value, highlighting the need for further studies to identify reliable predictors of outcome and recurrence.

title: Inter-week Variation in Movement Asymmetry at Trot in Cavalry Horses in Training.
abstract: The widespread use of objective motion analysis in lameness investigations has raised questions about whether movement asymmetries are caused by pain and when they are indicative of orthopaedic disease. The prevalence of motion asymmetries in horse populations in training is high, but longitudinal studies on variation in movement asymmetry are scarce. To investigate inter-week variation in movement symmetry during straight-line trot in horses in training over three weeks. Forty-nine cavalry horses in training were included in a longitudinal study. Horses were equipped with inertial measurement units, and vertical movement asymmetry of the head and pelvis during straight-line trot was measured weekly three times (2-4 runs per occasion). Asymmetry thresholds were 6 mm for the head (HDmin/HDmax) and 3 mm for the pelvis (PDmin/PDmax). Only five horses (10%, CI 95% 3-22%) were symmetric for all parameters on all the three measurement occasions. A high proportion of horses showed motion asymmetries, 76% (CI 95% 61-87%) during the first two weeks and 73% (CI 95% 59-85%) in the third week. Hindlimb push-off asymmetry (PDmax) was most common, seen in 61% (n=30) at least once and in 24% (n=12) on all occasions. Only five horses in this population trotted symmetrically throughout the study period. A high proportion of movement asymmetries was observed but there was substantial inter-week variation during three weeks of measurements. A hindlimb push-off asymmetry was the most common asymmetry, occurring in 61% of the horses. Longitudinal monitoring may help interpret the clinical significance of movement asymmetry.

title: Treatment of a concealed accessory pathway by radiofrequency catheter ablation in a horse.
abstract: Accessory pathways (APs) are myocardial bundles directly connecting the atria and the ventricles, bypassing the atrioventricular node-His-Purkinje system. Retrograde AP conduction in horses can result in orthodromic atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia or bradycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) can provide a permanent treatment by eliminating the retrograde conducting AP, but was previously unsuccessful in one case. To report the use of three-dimensional electro-anatomical mapping (3D EAM) to identify a concealed AP and treatment by RFCA in a horse. Retrospective case report. An irregular heart rhythm was detected in a 4-year-old, 518 kg Paint mare as an incidental finding. Frequent atrial depolarisations were identified in the ST segment with a fixed coupling interval to the preceding QRS complex on the ECG. A differential diagnosis of frequent premature atrial complexes displayed as bigeminy or a retrograde conduction along an AP was made. The presence of a retrograde conducting AP was confirmed by ventricular pacing, which resulted in 1:1 ventriculo-atrial activation. Three-dimensional EAM revealed the earliest atrial activation and thereby the atrial insertion of the AP in the caudal left atrium. Subsequent RFCA at 40 W eliminated AP conduction. Single case report. This case report describes the identification of an AP by 3D EAM and the first successful permanent treatment of a retrograde conducting AP by RFCA in an adult horse.

title: Correction to "The Impact of Systemic Treatment With Flunixin Meglumine on the Two Antiproteases Alpha-2-Macroglobulin (A2M) and Alpha-1-Antitrypsin (A1AT) in Equine Plasma and Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF)".
Physical Activity Intervention on Gross Motor and Social Skills in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors, affecting approximately 1 in 31 children in the United States. Children with ASD frequently demonstrate gross motor impairments and social skill deficits that compromise daily functioning and peer participation. Physical activity interventions have emerged as a promising non-pharmacological approach; however, no systematic review has focused simultaneously on both outcomes using exclusively RCT evidence from the past decade. To systematically review and synthesize RCT evidence on the effects of physical activity interventions on (1) gross motor skills and (2) social skills in children and adolescents with ASD aged 0-18 years. Systematic searches were conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science for RCTs published 2016-2026 in English. The review followed JBI methodology and PRISMA 2020 reporting standards. Quality assessment used the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and narrative synthesis followed the SWiM guideline. From 367 identified records, 275 remained after deduplication. After two-stage screening, 64 RCTs were included. Intervention types comprised general physical activity (n=16), dance/movement therapy (n=8), sport-based programs (n=8), exergaming/VR (n=6), aquatic therapy (n=5), yoga (n=4), equine therapy (n=4), and fundamental movement skills (n=4). Gross motor outcomes improved in 43 studies (67.2%) and social skill outcomes in 34 studies (53.1%). Risk of bias was "some concerns" in 30 studies (46.9%) and "high" in 34 studies (53.1%). Physical activity interventions demonstrate positive effects on both gross motor and social skills in children with ASD. Aquatic therapy showed the most consistent gross motor improvements, while equine therapy and martial arts demonstrated the strongest social outcomes. Interventions of ≥3 sessions/week over ≥8 weeks yielded the largest effects. Findings support integration of structured physical activity into multidisciplinary pediatric care for ASD. 10.17605/OSF.IO/KV9SM.

title: Adverse effects of a superovulatory regimen of equine chorionic gonadotropin and gonadotropin-releasing hormone on embryo implantation in mice.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: Although equine chorionic gonadotropin (eCG) combined with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is known to improve reproductive rates by increasing the numbers of ovulating oocytes, the actions of these hormones on embryo implantation have not been elucidated. We herein eliminated the effects of embryos by performing embryo transfer and elucidated the effects on embryo implantation after hormonal treatment. The recipient mice were allocated to four groups, including control, eCG, GnRH, and eCG + GnRH groups. Well-developed blastocysts were transferred into recipients, and implantation sites were counted five days after embryo transfer. Our results revealed that embryo implantation rates in the eCG and eCG + GnRH groups were significantly lower than GnRH and control groups; eCG and eCG + GnRH groups didn't differ, and the implantation rate was the lowest in the eCG + GnRH group. When we evaluated estrogen and progesterone concentrations in four groups on embryonic day 0.5 to embryonic day 3.5, we noted that serum estrogen levels in eCG + GnRH group were significantly higher than the other groups, while progesterone levels were significantly lower than the control group, and that the progesterone/estrogen ratio was significantly reduced relative to the control group. Finally, the expression of the endometrial receptivity-related Lif gene was significantly diminished in the eCG + GnRH and eCG groups compared to the other groups. These results suggest that eCG combined with GnRH as a super-ovulatory regimen reduced mouse embryo implantation rates via an estrogen-mediated impairment of endometrial receptivity.

title: Serological evidence of high West Nile virus exposure in equines of Oman and analysis of associated risk factors.
abstract: West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne pathogen capable of causing encephalitis in humans and horses. Horses share mosquito vectors with humans and seroconvert following infection, making them valuable sentinel species for WNV surveillance. In this cross-sectional study, 453 equines from 52 locations across eight governorates of northern Oman were screened for anti-WNV IgG antibodies using a competitive ELISA, with IgG-positive samples further tested for IgM to detect recent infection. Overall apparent seroprevalence was 47.0% (95% CI 42.3-51.8%; 213/453). No IgM-positive samples were detected, indicating past rather than recent exposure. Multivariable logistic regression identified age and proximity to surface water as independent risk factors for seropositivity: odds increased with age (5.1-10 years: OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.59-3.85; >10 years: OR 4.40, 95% CI 2.56-7.55) and with closer proximity to water bodies (≤ 200 m: OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.27-3.98; 201-500 m: OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.21-4.88). No significant associations were found with breed, sex, or interspecies contact. These findings indicate substantial WNV exposure among equines in northern Oman and support their role as sentinel hosts at the animal-human interface, underscoring the need for integrated One Health surveillance of WNV and related orthoflaviviruses.

title: Research into vitamin E supplementation to combat oxidative stress in equines: A mini-review.
abstract: Oxidative stress is a concern in performance horses because intense and prolonged exercise increases production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in contracting skeletal muscle. Low ROS concentrations support normal muscle function and adaptation, but excess ROS can damage lipids, proteins, and DNA. Vitamin E, particularly alpha tocopherol, is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that interrupts lipid peroxidation by donating a hydrogen atom to lipid peroxyl radicals. This mini-review summarizes recent equine research on vitamin E supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Results are variable and appear to depend on dose, form, baseline vitamin E status, and exercise intensity. Natural RRR-α-tocopherol raised serum alpha tocopherol more than synthetic vitamin E, and a water-dispersible liquid formulation rapidly increased serum concentrations in horses with subclinical deficiency, although studies of these formulations are small and limited to subclinical or healthy horses. The review also covers vitamin E metabolism, the role of alpha tocopherol transfer proteins in equine neurologic disease, forage sources of vitamin E, the interaction of vitamin E with selenium, and daily rhythms of oxidative parameters. Further controlled studies with larger sample sizes are needed to define the optimal dose, form, and timing of vitamin E supplementation in performance horses.

title: Differential expression of miRNAs in experimental metacarpal and lumbar wounds in horses.
abstract: Distal limb wounds in horses exhibit delayed healing and a predisposition to exuberant granulation tissue (EGT) formation, associated with hypoxia and persistent inflammation. The involvement of microRNAs (miRNAs) in this process in this species remains poorly elucidated. To determine the differential expression of miRNAs in experimental metacarpal and lumbar wounds in horses, based on the hypothesis that distinct anatomical regions present specific post-transcriptional regulation profiles. A controlled experimental study involving four healthy adult horses. Standardized cutaneous wounds (2 × 2 cm) were created in the lumbar and metacarpal regions of the same animal. Biopsies were collected 21 days post-injury. RNA was extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples and subsequently analyzed by microarray (Affymetrix miRNA 4.1 Array). Differential expressions were determined by analysis of variance with empirical moderation, considering p +2. Nucleotide sequences and human orthologs were obtained from the miRBase platform. Six miRNAs were differentially expressed in the metacarpus compared with the lumbar region. eca-miR-205 showed higher expression in the metacarpus . The others demonstrated lower expression in the metacarpus: eca-miR-127 , eca-miR-379 , eca-miR-335 , eca-miR-376c , and eca-miR-487b. This study demonstrates, for the first time, the differentially expressed miRNAs involved in wound healing in horses and highlights differences in miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional regulation between the lumbar and metacarpal regions. These findings expand the understanding of the differences in healing between these regions, suggesting that miRNAs could be studied as potential biomarkers for hard-to-heal wounds.

title: The Pharmaceutical Exposome: Micro- and Nanoplastic Leaching From Primary Packaging and Its Toxicological Impact on the Human Gut Microbiota.
abstract: The pharmaceutical exposome encompasses human exposure to non-biological contaminants associated with medicinal products, including microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) potentially released from primary packaging. Materials such as high-density polyethylene, polyvinyl chloride, and polyethylene terephthalate may contribute particles during storage, transport, and handling, particularly in liquid formulations. Experimental and preclinical studies suggest that MPs/NPs can alter gut microbiota composition, reduce beneficial bacterial populations, impair short-chain fatty acid production, and promote inflammatory responses. Reported cellular effects include oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, disruption of intestinal tight junctions, and lysosomal damage. MPs/NPs may also provide surfaces for biofilm formation and interact with active pharmaceutical ingredients through proposed "Trojan Horse" mechanisms, although the pharmaceutical relevance of these processes remains uncertain. Chemical constituents associated with packaging, including phthalates and residual catalysts, may provide additional exposure pathways with potential inflammatory or endocrine-disrupting effects. Pediatric patients, individuals receiving long-term medications, and patients with pre-existing gastrointestinal dysbiosis may warrant particular attention because of potential biological susceptibility or repeated exposure. Analytical characterization remains challenging because pharmaceutical matrices are complex and highly susceptible to contamination, requiring complementary spectroscopic and mass-spectrometric approaches with rigorous quality control. Importantly, direct human evidence specifically linking pharmaceutical packaging-derived MPs/NPs to clinically relevant exposure or adverse health outcomes remains sparse. Current evidence should therefore be interpreted cautiously, with greater emphasis on source-specific human exposure assessment, standardized analytical methods, longitudinal studies, evidence-based risk evaluation, and harmonized regulatory frameworks.

title: Radiographic abnormalities in the fetlock joints of equestrian horses in Tehran province, Iran.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: Disorders and injuries of the fetlock joint, encompassing both bone and soft tissue, are significant causes of limb pain and lameness in horses. Over time, these conditions can lead to joint dysfunction and a diminished quality of life. This study aimed to identify fetlock joint disorders using radiological examinations conducted during pre-purchase evaluations of horses and to evaluate the influence of age and sex on their incidence rates. 100 horses were selected from equestrian centers in Tehran Province during 2017 - 2020. As part of pre-purchase examinations, standard radiographic projections of the fetlock joints of all four limbs were obtained. Among the 100 horses examined, 28 showed no abnormalities in the fetlock joint, while 72 exhibited at least one disorder. Osteoarthritis was the most frequently observed condition, with an incidence of 26.75%, followed by soft tissue swelling (15.80%), medial and lateral proximal sesamoiditis (6.00%), osteochondritis dissecans (7.50%) and avulsion fractures (1.50%). Other disorders accounted for less than 5.00% of cases. The prevalence of disorders was significantly higher in the forelimbs compared to the hindlimbs, while no significant difference was found between male and female horses. The findings of this study underscored the importance of conducting pre-purchase radiographic examinations, particularly of the fetlock joints in both forelimbs and hindlimbs. These evaluations are crucial for identifying potential bone complications and for assessing the prognosis of a horse athletic performance.

title: Therapeutic effects of ethanol extract of propolis on experimental cutaneous candidiasis in horse.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: Candida albicans is a commensal opportunistic yeast colonizing the skin and mucosal surfaces of humans and animals, which, under specific predisposing conditions, can proliferate excessively and lead to clinical manifestations of candidiasis. The widespread prophylactic and therapeutic use of antifungal agents has led to the emergence of drug-resistant strains, necessitating the exploration of novel therapeutic alternatives. Considering the clinical and conformational significance of equine skin health, the present study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of ethanol extract of propolis in an experimental model of cutaneous candidiasis in horses. In 2022, two clinically healthy, six-year-old female horses (approximately 400 kg) were selected for the study. Immunosuppression was induced using dexamethasone and four intradermal inoculation sites were created on the shaved thoracic and flank regions of both lateral aspects using C. albicans (PTCC: 5027) suspension (5 × 10⁶ CFU mL-1). The experimental sites on the right thorax were treated with ethanol extract of propolis while those on the left thorax received topical nystatin. Lesions on the right flank were treated with glycerin as a vehicle control, and lesions on the left flank were left untreated. Cutaneous candidiasis was successfully induced within five days post-inoculation. Clinical resolution was observed following five days of treatment with ethanol extract of propolis, whereas, nystatin required eight days to achieve complete lesion resolution. The findings of this study suggested that topical ethanol extract of propolis demonstrated superior efficacy in accelerating the resolution of C. albicans-induced cutaneous lesions in horses compared to nystatin.

title: A rare case report of active Babesia caballi infection in a mare from Gonbad-e-Kavus, Iran.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: Babesia caballi is a tick-borne protozoan parasite responsible for causing equine babesiosis, a disease with considerable variation in prevalence across different regions of the world. This report presented a confirmed case of B. caballi infection in a three-year-old mare originating from Gonbad-e Kavus, Iran, highlighting the clinical, laboratory and diagnostic aspects of the disease. The affected mare showed classical clinical signs including persistent fever, generalized weakness, tachycardia and pale mucous membranes, which are indicative of systemic infection and anemia. Laboratory evaluations revealed evidence of hepatic and renal compromise as well as hematological parameters consistent with active inflammatory processes. Microscopic examination of blood smears and molecular techniques such as PCR were employed to confirm the presence of B. caballi, while simultaneously excluding co-infections with other common equine pathogens including Theileria equi and Anaplasma phagocytophilum. This case underscored the critical need to combine conventional diagnostic approaches with molecular methods to achieve accurate detection, effective treatment and appropriate management strategies for equine babesiosis in endemic regions.

title: Case Report: Histological study of gastric leiomyosarcoma in a young horse.
abstract: During the necropsy of a 4-year-old male horse, a protruding mass was detected in the nonglandular region of the stomach. It was roughly oval in shape with a brown surface and a grayish-white cut surface. The tumor was attached to part of the stomach wall. Histologically, the tumor cells were derived from the smooth muscle layer. Tumor cells showed various morphologies and nuclear atypia. Mitotic figures were rare. Some of the tumor cells resembled smooth muscle cells. Tumor cells were seen in blood vessels within the tumor. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells were positive for alpha smooth muscle actin antibody and were negative for CD117 (c-kit) antibody. Based on these findings, the tumor was diagnosed as leiomyosarcoma derived from gastric smooth muscle.

title: Functional peptide therapeutics for veterinary osteoarthritis: mechanisms, delivery systems, and translational priorities.
abstract: Veterinary osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic whole-joint disorder that causes pain, gait impairment, reduced activity, and diminished quality of life in companion and performance animals. Current multimodal management includes weight control, rehabilitation, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, prostaglandin E2 EP4 receptor antagonists, anti-nerve growth factor monoclonal antibodies, intra-articular therapies, and nutraceuticals. Although these interventions improve pain and function, they generally do not restore the cartilage extracellular matrix or provide sustained disease modification. Functional peptides have emerged as promising candidates because of their potential to suppress inflammation, inhibit matrix degradation, promote chondrogenesis, target damaged cartilage, and support sustained or targeted delivery. This narrative review evaluated the pathobiological rationale, veterinary evidence, peptide classes, delivery technologies, pharmacological requirements, and translational barriers relevant to veterinary OA. Targeted literature searches and qualitative evidence appraisal focused on clinical relevance, peptide mechanisms, delivery strategies, species-specific limitations, and the distinction between nutritional collagen hydrolysates and sequence-defined therapeutic peptides. Oral bioactive collagen peptides currently provide the most direct clinical evidence in naturally occurring canine and equine OA. However, the principal canine trial was limited by modest sample size and duration, predominantly symptomatic rather than structural outcomes, and manufacturer support. Thus, the available evidence supports potential adjunctive clinical benefit rather than a disease-modifying claim. Sequence-defined hyaluronan-binding, bone morphogenetic protein receptor-mimetic, collagen-binding, collagen-hybridizing, and cartilage-targeting peptides have demonstrated mechanistic or delivery advantages in cell, tissue, rodent, and selected large-animal studies, but target-species pharmacokinetic and clinical validation remains limited. A credible development pathway should integrate target-specific activity, protease stability, immunogenicity, manufacturability, species-appropriate delivery, joint exposure, repeated-dose safety, objective gait and activity outcomes, and structural endpoints. Functional peptides are unlikely to replace multimodal care in the near term but may become valuable adjunctive platforms and contribute to future disease-modifying strategies when biological activity is supported by demonstrated joint exposure, structural protection, and rigorous comparative trials.

title: Two-dimensional ultrasonography study of normal ocular structures in Turkmen horse.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: Ocular ultrasonography is a safe, painless and non-invasive diagnostic tool that provides veterinarians with detailed images of the eye and surrounding structures. This study evaluated 30 clinically healthy Turkmen horses, divided into two groups as Group 1: under 36 months (3 males, 8 females), and Group 2: 36 months and older (8 males, 11 females). Significant differences in several ocular parameters were identified across different age groups in Turkmen horses. Specifically, the mean intercanthal distance, globe diameter, ciliary body volume and area, iris thickness, corpora nigra distance, volume and area, vitreous chamber and retinal/choroidal/scleral composite size demonstrated statistically significant variations between age categories. No significant differences were detected between sexes within any of the age groups for above measured parameters. Of the ocular parameters evaluated, only anterior chamber depth, central lens thickness and ciliary body thickness demonstrated statistically significant differences based on both sex and age. The average corneal thickness of the left and right eyes, as measured in sagittal and dorsal planes, was similar in both male horses under 36 months and those 36 months or older when compared to their respective female counterparts. No significant differences were observed between measurements of the left and right eyes, nor were there significant discrepancies between sagittal and dorsal measurements. These findings provided a baseline for understanding normal ocular ultrasonographic features in Turkmen horses and might aid in diagnosis and management of ocular diseases specific to this breed.

title: Keratinolytic activity of Stenotrophomonas rhizophila and Bacillus spp. as keratin waste biodegradation.
abstract: Waste feathers pose a significant environmental challenge due to their resistance and the large amounts produced by the poultry industry. In this study, we isolated and characterized a novel keratinolytic strain, Stenotrophomonas rhizophila SMT, from horse feces and evaluated its feather-degrading ability and production of soluble keratin hydrolysates. Additionally, its keratinolytic ability was assessed along with both Bacillus subtilis and Bacillus cereus. S. rhizophila SMT was identified by biochemical profiling and confirmed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, which showed 99% similarity to S. rhizophila. Primary screening on skim-milk agar and egg-yolk agar showed their keratinolytic activity. Subsequent cultivation in minimal salt media with chicken feathers confirmed and quantified their feather degradation efficiency by using the Bradford assay. After 13 days, S. rhizophila SMT produced 0.535 mg/mL soluble protein, while B. subtilis and B. cereus produced 0.615 mg/mL and 1.215 mg/mL, respectively. S. rhizophila SMT is a safe and non-pathogenic candidate despite producing less soluble protein than B. cereus. This makes it an eco-friendly choice for management of feather wastes, especially when biosafety is a priority.

title: Dermacentor reticulatus as a vector of microsporidian infections: A cross-sectional analysis in the Czech Republic.
abstract: Dermacentor reticulatus is an emerging tick species in Central Europe with growing significance as a vector of various pathogens. This study reports, for the first time, the presence of human-pathogenic microsporidia in D. reticulatus ticks collected from South Moravia, Czech Republic. Ticks trapped by flagging from vegetation at ten various sites in the Czech Republic were homogenized and tested for presence of microsporidial DNA using PCR and sequencing, and the microsporidial load was quantified by qPCR. A total of 277 ticks were analyzed using molecular methods, revealing microsporidian DNA in 7.58 % of samples. Several zoonotic species and genotypes were identified, including Encephalitozoon cuniculi genotypes I and II, E. intestinalis, and Enterocytozoon bieneusi genotypes D, horse 1, and Peru 8. Dual infections were observed in two ticks. Spore burden ranged from 102 to 103 spores per tick. Although spore loads were relatively low, the presence of microsporidia in ticks indicates a potential role for D. reticulatus as a mechanical or biological vector. Our findings highlight the need for further investigation into the ecological and public health implications of microsporidia transmission by ticks.

title: Computed tomography anatomy of the pony thorax and abdomen and an example of a clinical application.
abstract: In veterinary medicine, computed tomography (CT) is a valuable diagnostic tool that provides detailed cross-sectional images with higher contrast resolution than conventional radiography. However, owing to the large body-size of horses, CT has been primarily limited in equine veterinary practice to imaging of the head, neck, and extremities, as imaging studies of the thoracic and abdominal cavities are not possible with standard gantry size in medium-to-large horses. In this study, we aimed to characterise the normal thoracic and abdominal anatomy of ponies using CT and to describe an example of the potential clinical applications of abdominal CT. CT examination of two ponies was performed in dorsal recumbency using a helical 16-slice multidetector scanner with a 90 cm-diameter gantry. The normal anatomy of these cavities was described and compared with anatomical cross-sections, and a clinical case involving colic surgery was analysed. Most of the thoracic and abdominal organs in the anatomical section were identifiable, and the use of these images as a reference assisted well in the interpretation of the clinical case scans. The advanced imaging technique aided in surgical planning. In the case involving colic surgery, no evidence of thick-walled intestinal segments was found on CT, but contents including gas, fluid, different types of ingests, and sand were identified preoperatively. Nerves or serous membranes (except for the spinal cord) could not be clearly identified on native CT images. CT was useful for clinical diagnosis, but the small number of cases included in the study is a limitation that should be acknowledged.

title: Equine trophoblastic vesicles: ultrastructural and histologic features, extracellular vesicle production, and hormone secretion.
abstract: Maternal recognition of pregnancy (MRP) in mares remains incompletely understood, and trophoblastic vesicles (TRV) may provide a useful in vitro model to study trophoblast cell contributions to MRP. The objectives of this study were to characterize the structural, ultrastructural, and functional features of TRV derived from Day (D) 10 and D14 equine conceptuses. Equine conceptuses were collected transcervically, fragmented, and cultured to generate TRV. Vesicle morphology and ultrastructure were assessed by light microscopy, transmission and scanning electron microscopy, and lipid staining. The hormones estradiol-17β and prostaglandin E (PGE) secretion were measured in TRV conditioned media, and extracellular vesicles (EV) were isolated and characterized. Embryo fragments spontaneously formed TRV, spherical vesicular structures composed of one to three cell layers, and displayed ultrastructural features characteristic of trophoblast cells, including microvilli, tight junctions, endoplasmic reticulum, and abundant lipid droplets. TRV secreted estradiol-17β and PGE in a time-dependent manner, with D10 TRV showing increasing hormone production during culture. In addition, TRV released small EV. Post-thaw survival following cryopreservation was 10%. In conclusion, TRV retain key morphological, ultrastructural, and functional characteristics of the equine trophoblast and represent a promising in vitro model for investigating aspects of trophoblast cell function, particularly during early conceptus development.

title: Seasonal, age- and fertility-related dynamics of serum insulin-like peptide 3 and anti-Müllerian hormone concentrations in stallions.
abstract: Insulin-like peptide 3 (INSL3) regulates the transabdominal phase of testicular descent in male mouse fetuses and is a biomarker of Leydig cell functionality. However, equine research remains limited. Although anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) is a reliable diagnostic tool for equine cryptorchidism, its potential as a fertility biomarker remains unexplored. Therefore, we aimed to assess the biomarker potential of circulating INSL3, AMH, and testosterone in post-pubertal stallions. First, monthly blood samples were collected from 10 Thoroughbred stallions (age: 9.4 ± 1.6 years) for 12 months. Additionally, single-point samples were collected from 16 stallions (5-30 years) during breeding and non-breeding seasons for age-related analysis. Second, breeding (May) and non-breeding (January) samples were obtained from 25 stallions (age: 10.2 ± 4.5 years) categorized by conception rates per cycle. Serum concentrations were quantified using a time-resolved fluorescence immunoassay (for INSL3), a commercial chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassay (for AMH), and an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (for testosterone). The effects of circulating INSL3 and testosterone levels peaked with increasing day lengths; nadirs were observed over short day lengths. AMH lacked monthly fluctuations. However, all hormone levels decreased during non-breeding season. Age was not significantly correlated with hormone concentrations in post-pubertal breeding stallions. Contrastingly, correlations between breeding season INSL3-AMH, inter-seasonal testosterone, and AMH were observed. However, no hormonal differences were observed between fertility groups. Thus, INSL3 exhibits manipulatable seasonal dynamics, and may be useful for screening seasonal reproductivity. INSL3-AMH breeding season coordination revealed Leydig-Sertoli interplay in stallions. Nevertheless, circulating INSL3, AMH, and testosterone alone appear insufficient as fertility biomarkers in stallions.

title: Histidine-51 Facilitates the Conformational Change and Deprotonation of Horse Liver Alcohol Dehydrogenase-NAD+ Complexes.
abstract: Structural studies suggest that His-51 in wild-type horse liver alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH1E) facilitates proton transfer between the hydroxyl group of a ligand bound to the catalytic zinc and bulk solvent. Previous work showed that the Gln-51 substitution increases the pK values for pH dependencies for various enzymatic reactions by about 1.5 units, and stopped-flow studies on the binding of NAD+ and pyrazole suggested that the equilibrium position for the global conformational change of the enzyme-NAD+ complex became disfavored by 1000-fold. That conclusion needed confirmation. Here, X-ray crystallography of six ternary complexes of H51Q ADH with NAD+ and pyrazole, caprate, 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol, or 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl alcohol, and NADH and water or N-cyclohexylformamide shows that all complexes have the same closed conformation as wild-type ADH. Gln-51 fits in the region occupied by His-51 and does not affect the positions of bound coenzymes or inhibitors that coordinate to the catalytic zinc. Stopped-flow studies show that the rate-limiting formation of ternary complexes with H51Q ADH and NAD+ depends upon deprotonation of the ligands that bind to the catalytic zinc (pyrazole or 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol). Furthermore, the binding of NAD+ and trifluoroethanol monitored by fluorescence and proton release show that the H51Q substitution disfavors the conformational change by about 3-fold as compared to wild-type ADH. The pK values of the enzyme-NAD+ complexes with water and other zinc ligands increase because His-51 no longer facilitates the deprotonation. The roles of the zinc-water and His-51 in the mechanism are exposed.

title: Managing equine asthma: Owner adherence, practical constraints and environmental protocol evaluation.
abstract: Adherence to recommendations for environmental management is central to equine asthma (EA) treatment. Reasons for non-adherence warrant further investigation. To: (1) evaluate adherence to recommendations for environmental changes, identify reasons for incomplete implementation, assess changes in clinical signs and medication use; (2) evaluate owner acceptability, practicality and perceived usefulness of a structured stable-side protocol. (1) Retrospective online survey and (2) prospective onsite testing with owners of EA-affected horses. (1) Online survey on implementation of standardised recommendations, clinical progression and medication use; and (2) environmental protocol evaluation during stable visits. Seventeen of 40 horses still received dry hay and 13/40 were bedded on straw. Reasons for non-implementation included time, financial and infrastructural constraints, boarding stable restrictions, group housing, weather dependence, use of self-produced roughage, perceived ineffectiveness and individual horse preferences. Owners reported that overall clinical impression had improved and the proportion of coughing horses decreased from 88% to 55% (p < 0.001, OR = 0.07, 95% CI 0.002-0.47, n = 40). The other clinical outcomes did not reach the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. Twenty-two horses were still coughing, and 7/40 had received medication within the previous 3 months. All interviewed owners found the environmental protocol helpful, 11 reviewed it again and 5 used it for discussion with others. Use of small convenience samples, lack of a control group and potential selection and recall bias. Owner non-adherence arose from diverse and often structural constraints. The environmental protocol was well accepted by owners and helped to structure discussions on risk factors.

title: Browse Preferences, Intake, and Feeding Behaviour of Domestic Donkeys Provided Native Hedgerow Species.
journal: Journal of applied animal welfare science : JAAWS
abstract: Donkeys (Equus asinus) are mixed feeders that browse and graze, with woody vegetation contributing substantially to free-roaming diets. However, domestic donkeys in the United Kingdom are typically kept on improved pastures with limited browse access. This study investigated browse preferences, intake, and time budgets when native hedgerow species were provided. Two complementary studies were conducted. In study one, hazel, field maple, hawthorn, and bramble were offered to miniature and standard herds across six cafeteria trials per herd, and biomass consumption and bite rate were recorded. In study two, browse was provided to three pairs, and foraging behaviour was recorded using instantaneous scan sampling. Proportional biomass consumption differed significantly among species, with miniature donkeys preferring hazel. Mean intake over 15 minutes was 445.0 g per standard donkey and 182.5 g per miniature donkey. During the time-budget study, donkeys spent 21% of observed time browsing, including consuming twigs and stripping branches and logs. Findings demonstrate preferences for hedgerow species and an emphasis on browsing when opportunities are available. Incorporating woody browse, particularly hazel, into domestic donkey management may support natural foraging behaviours. .

title: Association of facial expression, biochemistry, and microRNAs with lameness in endurance horses.
abstract: Lameness is common in endurance horses. Conventional gait-based assessment may not fully capture its various aspects. Facial expression scales can provide complementary, non-locomotor indicators of lameness-related pain. To evaluate the performance of facial expression scales Horse Grimace Scale (HGS) and Equine Utrecht University Scale for Facial Assessment of Pain (EQUUS-FAP) for assessing pain-related lameness in endurance horses and their associations with the American Association of Equine Practitioners (AAEP) lameness grading system, biochemical, and molecular markers.
